newsitem.title: GERMANY: Criticism of Bonn grows on German jobless crisis.
newsitem.headline: Criticism of Bonn grows on German jobless crisis.

text.p: Criticism grew on Saturday of the German government's failure to tackle the country's growing numbers of jobless, which have hit levels not seen since the depression of the early 1930s.

Germany's top trade union official declared that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government was incapable of confronting the issue and, according to a poll for a television station, two-thirds of Germans agreed.
Dieter Schulte, chairman of the German Federation of Trade Unions (DGB), said the government would not be able to produce a turnaround in the jobs market in time to win re-election next year.
"This government will not manage to steer the ship back on course before the elections in 1998," he said in a summary of an interview for Sunday's Tagesspiegel newspaper.
Schulte said it was now time "to look around for other majorities outside the current coalition."
His comments came after Kohl fired speculation about whether he would seek re-election by saying that he had not yet made up his mind.

Critics blame austerity measures introduced by Kohl's government for the continuing rise in unemployment. The number of people out of work jumped by more than half a million in January to 4.66 million.

Kohl contends that the cost-cutting measures, which are designed to shave billions of marks from government deficits, are necessary if Germany is to meet criteria for entry into the single European currency.

He also insists that the German employment market is in need of wide reform, accusing Germans, who enjoy a range of social benefits and favourable working conditions, of having got too used to the easy life.
But a poll conducted for the N-TV commercial television channel said 69 percent of those interviewed believed that the government's employment policies were incorrect.
Three-quarters thought that unemployment could be reduced with proper job creation measures, but a similar number thought the situation would only get worse in coming months.
